newsitem.title: IRAN: Cash shortages hamper Iran power projects-official.
newsitem.headline: Cash shortages hamper Iran power projects-official.

text.p: Shortages in government funding are hampering projects to raise Iran's annual power output by 7,000 megawatts by March 2000, a cabinet minister said in remarks published on Thursday.

Deputy Energy Minister Mohammad Mallaki told the daily Resalat that state banks had so far only paid out 330 billion rials ($189 million) of the 970 billion rials earmarked for power projects in the Iranian year which ends on March 20.

The funds were needed if Iran wanted to meet a seven percent annual rise in power consumption by increasing output to 27,000 MW within its Second Five Year Plan which ends in March 2000, Mallaki was quoted as saying.
He said the payments were delayed because of a disagreement between the banks and the state Plan and Budget Organisation.

Rural electrification projects had so far received 120 billion rials out of a total budgeted 180 billion rials in the current Iranian year, while last year only 120 billion rials out of 300 billions were paid out, Mallaki added. ($1=1,750 rials at the rate used for state bugdet accounts)
